newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand appoints new army chief.
newsitem.headline: Thailand appoints new army chief.

text.p: Thailand promoted General Chetta Thanajaro on Tuesday to the powerful post of army commander in chief to replace General Pramon Phalasi, who retires at the end of this month, a government spokesman said.

Chief of joint military staff General Mongkol Ampornpisit was moved up to the ceremonial post of Thai Supreme Commander, the spokesman said. He would succeed outgoing General Viroj Saengsanit at the end of September.

Top military appointments are traditionally approved by King Bhumibol Adulyadej from a list presented to him by the prime minister. Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa had an audience with the king late on Monday.

Thailand's military has traditionally wielded strong influence over politics in a country which has seen 17 military coups or attempted coups since 1932 when the country switched to a parliamentary democracy from an absolute monarchy.
But political and diplomatic sources said the military role has dwindled in recent years, particularly after bloody pro-democracy street protests in Bangkok in 1992.

Military sources Banharn allowed Chetta, the choice of Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, to prevail in return for his support in parliament where Banharn faces an opposition-launched, no-confidence motion against him on Wednesday.
A senior official at government house said on Tuesday the prime minister did not alter the annual military promotion list proposed by Chavalit.

The premier's six-party coalition controls 209 of the 391 seats in parliament but political infighting within his government has made it vital for Banharn to actively seek out support from his coaltion partners, analysts said.
The new 58-year old army chief is an avid fan of sports, heading the Thai Amateur Boxing Association. He has vowed to keep the army out of politics.
An army general said the new army chief's appointment was supported by most senior military personnel.
"General Chetta, who has always distanced himself from politics, is the most appropriate choice to lead the army at this time," the general who declined to be identified said.

Air Chief Marshal Amorn Naewmalee, former air force chief of staff, was named to head the Thai air force while Admiral Vijit Chamnankarn, the deputy navy commander in chief, was promoted to the top naval post.
